targetText:
Centralisation of the means of production and
socialisation of labour at last reach a point where they become incompatible
with their capitalist integument. This integument is burst asunder. The
knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.
explanation: Capitalist accumulation leads to extreme centralization and socialized production. Eventually, the monopoly of capital becomes a fetter, leading to the socialist transformation.
summary: The expropriators are expropriated: extreme centralization and socialized production burst the capitalist integument, leading to socialist transformation.

targetText: The capitalist mode of appropriation, the result of the capitalist mode of production, produces capitalist private property. This is the first negation of individual private property, as founded on the labour of the proprietor. But capitalist production begets, with the inexorability of a law of Nature, its own negation. It is the negation of negation. This does not re-establish private property for the producer, but gives him individual property based on the acquisition of the capitalist era: i.e., on cooperation and the possession in common of the land and of the means of production.
summary: The negation of negation: capitalist socialization culminates in the expropriation of private property in favor of common ownership.
explanation: Individual private property based on self-earned labour was first negated by capitalist private property (the expropriation of many small producers by few capitalists). In turn, capitalist development inexorably socializes the labour process, leading to the negation of negation: the collective appropriation of the means of production by the associated working class.
context: Part VIII, Chapter 32: Historical Tendency of Capitalist Accumulation
